questionText:
Read the following occupational ergonomics case study and answer the questions that follow:

An occupational health audit at an export garment manufacturing factory reveals alarming health complaints among 200 sewing machine operators. Over 70% of female machine stitchers suffer from chronic Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs): lower back pain, neck stiffness, shoulder impingement, and Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the wrists. An ergonomics expert inspects the workstations and identifies severe ergonomic design flaws:
1. Sewing chairs are rigid wooden stools without lumbar backrests, forcing operators into continuous forward-stooped static kyphotic postures.
2. Foot pedals are fixed at awkward high angles, straining ankle joints and impeding venous blood return.
3. Poor task illumination (dim, flickering tubes) creates severe visual glare and eye strain, forcing operators to crane their necks close to needles.
The factory management executes an ergonomic redesign: introducing adjustable ergonomic chairs with lumbar support, adjustable angled foot pedals, glare-free LED needle task lights, and instituting mandatory 3-minute hourly stretch breaks.

Question: Why did repetitive manual fabric feeding and wrist bending cause Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the stitchers' hands?

options.text: Prolonged forearm pronation irritates the radial nerve sheath, restricting fluid movement through the cubital tunnel.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Static elbow hyperextension constricts the ulnar nerve canal, reducing sensory feedback along the dorsal digital branches.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Repetitive wrist flexion inflames surrounding flexor tendon sheaths, compressing the median nerve inside the carpal tunnel.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Biomechanics.

options.text: Excessive shoulder elevation compresses the brachial plexus, causing muscular atrophy in the palmar aponeurosis.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Carpal Tunnel Syndrome Biomechanics (Work, Livelihood and Career):
Repetitive awkward wrist flexion and extension inflate pressure within the anatomical carpal tunnel, inflaming the flexor tendon sheaths and compressing the median nerve. This causes the characteristic numbness, tingling, and discomfort of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome. Option B accurately states this pathophysiological mechanism, while the distractors present incorrect nerve pathways and anatomical structures.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
